title: Definiteness and open terms
summary: Definiteness concerns whether the parties’ commitment is clear enough for a court to identify the obligation, determine breach, and provide a remedy. An open term can sometimes be supplied without defeating the agreement.
notes:
The significance of a missing term depends on what the parties left open and what they intended. In Sun Printing, both future price and the period for which a price would apply remained unresolved. The court declined to impose the ongoing bargain urged by the buyer; the dissent offered a different reading. In Oglebay, a long relationship, a stated duration, and evidence of intended commitment supported supplying a price after specified pricing mechanisms failed.

Distinguish an agreement to agree later from a present commitment with a workable method for completing details. An external benchmark, established practice, course of performance, or governing gap-filler can make an obligation manageable. Those tools cannot automatically override an express decision to remain unbound until further agreement. The transaction’s purpose, wording, and history must justify the completion.
